# `silk/bench/process`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

Runs one program to its end and measures it: the time it took, the processor time it used,
and its peak memory.

## When to use
`silk.bench.bench` uses [`Process.time`](#Process.impl.time) for every sample of a command suite. Use it
directly to time a program in a harness of your own.

## Details
[`Process.time`](#Process.impl.time) starts the program, waits for it, and reads what the system counted for it
with `wait4`: processor time in user and kernel mode, and peak resident memory, over the
program and the children it waited for. The time from start to exit is read from the
`MonotonicClock`. The program's standard input, output and error are closed off, so printing
costs it nothing and does not reach the terminal.

[`Process.perform`](#Process.impl.perform) runs a program for its effect, such as a hook that clears a cache: the
program shares the terminal, and a failure is an error.

Both give the program the environment of this process and then the variables of the
[`Launch`](#Launch).

## Gotchas
- Processes can be measured on Linux with GNU libc and on macOS. On other systems
  [`Process.supported`](#Process.impl.supported) is false and both functions fail.
- Only Linux can limit a program to a number of processors.

Import as `Process` with `import silk.bench.process { Process }`.

<a id="Process.impl.floor"></a>

### Associated function `floor`

```silk
pub effect fn floor() -> u64
    ? &mut Allocator | &mut FileSystem
```

Returns the smallest peak memory [`Process.time`](#Process.impl.time) can report for a program started now, in
bytes, or 0 when there is none.

#### Details
On Linux a new process starts with the peak resident memory of the process that started
it, so a small program reads as this process's own peak. Other systems count a new
process from zero.

<a id="Process.impl.time"></a>

### Associated function `time`

```silk
pub effect fn time(launch: &Launch, cpus: u32, counted: bool) -> Timed
    ! TaskError | OutOfMemoryError
    ? &mut Allocator | &mut MonotonicClock
```

Runs `launch` to its end and returns what it cost. With `cpus` above 0, the program may
run only on that many processors, the first ones this process may use.

#### Details
A program that exits with a status other than 0, or that a signal ends, is not an error
here: the status is in the result, and the caller decides.

With `counted`, the run also reads the counters of the processor and of the kernel, on
Linux on x86_64 and aarch64: instructions, cycles, cache misses, branch misses and page
faults, all in user mode, for the program and the processes it starts, not
for this process. A counter the system does not offer is left out, so on another system,
or where the kernel refuses, `counts` is empty; a virtual machine often offers only the
last.

#### Errors
`TaskError` with status 127 if the program cannot be started, if `cpus` is more than
[`Process.processors`](#Process.impl.processors), or if this system cannot measure a process.

<a id="Process.impl.drive"></a>

### Associated function `drive`

```silk
pub effect fn drive(launch: &Launch, cpus: u32) -> Driven
    ! TaskError | OutOfMemoryError
    ? &mut Allocator
```

Starts `launch` with a pipe on its standard input and one on its standard output, and
returns at once. With `cpus` above 0, the program may use only that many processors.

#### Details
Both descriptors of the result are nonblocking, as `silk.bench.transport.StreamTransport`
expects. End the program with [`Process.finish`](#Process.impl.finish).

#### Errors
`TaskError` with status 127 if the program cannot be started, if `cpus` is more than
[`Process.processors`](#Process.impl.processors), or if this system cannot start such a program.

<a id="Process.impl.finish"></a>

### Associated function `finish`

```silk
pub effect fn finish(driven: &Driven) -> i64
    ! TaskError | OutOfMemoryError
    ? &mut Allocator
```

Closes the pipes of `driven`, which ends a program that reads its standard input to the
end, waits for the program, and returns its exit status, or -1 when a signal ended it.

#### Errors
`TaskError` with status 127 if the program's exit cannot be collected.

<a id="Process.impl.perform"></a>

### Associated function `perform`

```silk
pub effect fn perform(launch: &Launch) -> ()
    ! TaskError | OutOfMemoryError
    ? &mut Allocator
```

Runs `launch` to its end with the standard streams of this process, for its effect.

#### Errors
`TaskError` if the program cannot be started, exits with a status other than 0, which
becomes the error's status, or is ended by a signal.

<a id="Process.impl.text"></a>

### Associated function `text`

```silk
pub effect fn text(launch: &Launch) -> String
    ! OutOfMemoryError
    ? &mut Allocator
```

Returns `launch` as one line for a reader: the program, then its arguments, separated by
spaces. The line is for a report, not for a shell: nothing is quoted.

#### Errors
`OutOfMemoryError` if the `Allocator` cannot supply the text.

<a id="Process.impl.instructions"></a>

### Associated function `instructions`

```silk
pub fn instructions(profile: &[u8]) -> Option<u64>
```

Returns the number of instructions a Callgrind output file `profile` counted: the first
number of its `summary:` line, or of its `totals:` line when it has no summary. Returns
`None` if `profile` has neither line or the line has no number.

#### Examples
```silk
import silk.bench.process { Process }
import silk.core.option { Option }

pub fn main() -> i32 {
  let profile = b"events: Ir\nfn=main\n1 20\ntotals: 1840\nsummary: 1837 12\n"
  if let Option<u64>.Some { value } = Process.instructions(profile) {
    if value == 1837 {
      return 0
    }
  }
  return 1
}
```
